=== backend-deploy.yml
# Build, test, and deploy the backend.
#
# Runs on every push to main that changes a backend file. The commit is tested
# against a fresh PostgreSQL. Only if every test passes is it packed into
# dtm-backend.tar.gz, copied over the previous build in ~/dtm_build/ on the EC2
# host, and started there with start-dtm-service.sh.
#
# Repository settings this workflow reads
# (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions):
#
#   secret    EC2_SSH_KEY   private key (.pem) of the instance's key pair
#   variable  EC2_HOST      public DNS name or IP address of the instance
#   variable  EC2_USER      login user; optional, defaults to ec2-user
#   secret    LITELLM_API_KEY  neatlogs LiteLLM gateway key; written into the
#                              host's .env on every deploy when set
#
# The host must already hold ~/dtm_build/.env, and its security group must
# allow SSH (port 22) from GitHub-hosted runners.
name: Backend deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "datatracemind/**"
      - "etl/**"
      - "simulator/**"
      - "contracts/**"
      - "infra/**"
      - "tests/**"
      - "requirements.txt"
      - "pytest.ini"
      - "docker-compose.yml"
      - "start-dtm-service.sh"
      - ".github/workflows/backend-deploy.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build-test:
    name: Build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    services:
      # Same image and credentials as docker-compose.yml; tests/conftest.py
      # creates its own datatracemind_test database on this server.
      postgres:
        image: postgres:17-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: dtm_admin
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: REDACTED
          POSTGRES_DB: datatracemind
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U dtm_admin -d datatracemind"
          --health-interval 2s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Build
        run: python -m compileall -q datatracemind etl simulator

      - name: Test
        run: python -m pytest

      # Packed from the commit rather than the working tree, so nothing the
      # build or the tests left behind is shipped. start-dtm-service.sh
      # refuses an archive that lacks these paths.
      - name: Package
        run: |
          git archive --format=tar.gz -o dtm-backend.tar.gz HEAD \
            datatracemind etl simulator contracts infra requirements.txt docker-compose.yml

      - name: Keep the build
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: dtm-backend
          path: |
            dtm-backend.tar.gz
            start-dtm-service.sh
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to EC2
    needs: build-test
    # A manual run on another branch stops after the tests.
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # One deploy at a time. A newer one waits for the running one to finish.
    concurrency:
      group: backend-deploy
      cancel-in-progress: false
    env:
      EC2_HOST: ${{ vars.EC2_HOST }}
      EC2_USER: ${{ vars.EC2_USER || 'ec2-user' }}
    steps:
      - name: Download the build
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: dtm-backend

      - name: Set up SSH
        env:
          EC2_SSH_KEY: ${{ secrets.EC2_SSH_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [[ -z "$EC2_HOST" || -z "$EC2_SSH_KEY" ]]; then
            echo "::error::Set the EC2_HOST variable and the EC2_SSH_KEY secret in the repository settings."
            exit 1
          fi
          umask 077
          mkdir -p ~/.ssh
          printf '%s\n' "$EC2_SSH_KEY" > ~/.ssh/dtm_deploy
          # The runner is new on every run, so the host key is taken on first contact.
          if ! ssh-keyscan -T 15 "$EC2_HOST" > ~/.ssh/known_hosts 2>/dev/null || [[ ! -s ~/.ssh/known_hosts ]]; then
            echo "::error::Cannot reach $EC2_HOST on port 22. Check that the instance is running, that EC2_HOST is its current address, and that its security group allows SSH from GitHub Actions."
            exit 1
          fi
          cat > ~/.ssh/config <<EOF
          Host dtm
            HostName $EC2_HOST
            User $EC2_USER
            IdentityFile ~/.ssh/dtm_deploy
            IdentitiesOnly yes
            BatchMode yes
            ConnectTimeout 15
            ServerAliveInterval 30
          EOF

      - name: Replace the build on the host
        run: |
          ssh dtm 'mkdir -p dtm_build'
          scp dtm-backend.tar.gz start-dtm-service.sh dtm:dtm_build/

      # Keys kept as repository secrets are written into the host's .env, so
      # they need not be copied there by hand. A secret that is not set leaves
      # the .env line as it is. Values go over stdin, never on a command line.
      - name: Update settings on the host
        env:
          LITELLM_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.LITELLM_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          for name in LITELLM_API_KEY; do
            value="${!name}"
            [[ -n "$value" ]] || { echo "Secret $name is not set; keeping the host's value."; continue; }
            printf '%s' "$value" | ssh dtm "set -euo pipefail; umask 077
              value=\$(cat)
              touch dtm_build/.env && chmod 600 dtm_build/.env
              { grep -v '^$name=' dtm_build/.env || true; printf '%s=%s\n' '$name' \"\$value\"; } > dtm_build/.env.new
              mv dtm_build/.env.new dtm_build/.env"
            echo "Set $name in dtm_build/.env."
          done

      # A login shell, so the API inherits the same PATH (uv, the Codex CLI)
      # as when the script is run by hand. The script exits non-zero unless
      # /api/health answers, which fails this job.
      - name: Start the services
        run: ssh dtm 'bash -l dtm_build/start-dtm-service.sh'

=== db.py
"""PostgreSQL access and schema management.

Two credentials exist. The application role owns every schema and is used by
the simulator, the ETL, and the repair executor. The read-only role can only
SELECT from the source, the analytics target, and the transform history; it
is the one handed to the investigation tools, so nothing an agent calls can
write, and nothing it calls can read DataTraceMind's own state.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from collections.abc import Iterator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from datetime import date, datetime
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import Any

import psycopg
from psycopg import sql
from psycopg.conninfo import conninfo_to_dict
from psycopg.rows import dict_row
from psycopg.types.json import set_json_dumps

from datatracemind.config import SQL_DIR, get_settings

ANALYTICS_SCHEMA = "analytics"
STAGING_SCHEMA = "staging"
SOURCE_SCHEMA = "oltp"
READONLY_SCHEMAS = (SOURCE_SCHEMA, ANALYTICS_SCHEMA, "pipeline")
READONLY_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000


def to_jsonable(value: Any) -> Any:
    """Convert database values into plain JSON types."""
    if isinstance(value, Decimal):
        return float(value)
    if isinstance(value, (datetime, date)):
        return value.isoformat()
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {str(k): to_jsonable(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple, set)):
        return [to_jsonable(v) for v in value]
    return value


set_json_dumps(lambda obj: json.dumps(to_jsonable(obj)))


_writes_forbidden = False


def forbid_write_connections() -> None:
    """Make this process unable to open a read-write connection.

    Called by the tool server, which runs code on behalf of a model.
    """
    global _writes_forbidden
    _writes_forbidden = True


@contextmanager
def connect(*, readonly: bool = False, autocommit: bool = False) -> Iterator[psycopg.Connection]:
    """Open a connection that commits on success and rolls back on error."""
    if _writes_forbidden and not readonly:
        raise PermissionError("this process may only open read-only database connections")
    settings = get_settings()
    if readonly:
        url = settings.readonly_database_url
        options = (
            "-c default_transaction_read_only=on "
            f"-c statement_timeout={READONLY_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS}"
        )
    else:
        url = settings.database_url
        options = None
    with psycopg.connect(url, row_factory=dict_row, autocommit=autocommit, options=options) as conn:
        yield conn


def fetch_all(query: str | sql.Composable, params: Any = None, *, readonly: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    with connect(readonly=readonly) as conn:
        return conn.execute(query, params).fetchall()


def fetch_one(query: str | sql.Composable, params: Any = None, *, readonly: bool = False) -> dict | None:
    with connect(readonly=readonly) as conn:
        return conn.execute(query, params).fetchone()


def execute(query: str | sql.Composable, params: Any = None) -> None:
    with connect() as conn:
        conn.execute(query, params)


def _read_sql(name: str) -> str:
    return (SQL_DIR / name).read_text()


def create_target_schema(conn: psycopg.Connection, schema: str) -> None:
    """Create the analytics tables in `schema` (idempotent)."""
    if schema not in (ANALYTICS_SCHEMA, STAGING_SCHEMA):
        raise ValueError(f"not a target schema: {schema}")
    conn.execute(_read_sql("target.sql").replace("__TARGET__", schema))


def rebuild_staging(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> None:
    """Drop and recreate the staging target so each validation starts empty."""
    conn.execute(sql.SQL("DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS {} CASCADE").format(sql.Identifier(STAGING_SCHEMA)))
    create_target_schema(conn, STAGING_SCHEMA)


def _ensure_readonly_role(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> None:
    info = conninfo_to_dict(get_settings().readonly_database_url)
    role, password = info["user"], info["password"]
    exists = conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = %s", (role,)).fetchone()
    verb = sql.SQL("ALTER") if exists else sql.SQL("CREATE")
    conn.execute(
        sql.SQL("{} ROLE {} LOGIN PASSWORD {}").format(verb, sql.Identifier(role), sql.Literal(password))
    )
    for schema in READONLY_SCHEMAS:
        conn.execute(
            sql.SQL("GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA {s} TO {r}; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA {s} TO {r}").format(
                s=sql.Identifier(schema), r=sql.Identifier(role)
            )
        )


def ensure_schema() -> None:
    """Create every schema, table, and role that is missing (idempotent)."""
    with connect() as conn:
        # Concurrent callers (tests, API startup) would otherwise race on
        # CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS, which is not atomic in PostgreSQL.
        conn.execute("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('dtm_schema'))")
        conn.execute(_read_sql("oltp.sql"))
        conn.execute(_read_sql("pipeline.sql"))
        create_target_schema(conn, ANALYTICS_SCHEMA)
        conn.execute(_read_sql("dtm.sql"))
        _ensure_readonly_role(conn)


def drop_all() -> None:
    """Remove all demo data and state. Used only by the demo reset."""
    with connect() as conn:
        conn.execute("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('dtm_schema'))")
        for schema in (SOURCE_SCHEMA, ANALYTICS_SCHEMA, STAGING_SCHEMA, "pipeline", "dtm"):
            conn.execute(sql.SQL("DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS {} CASCADE").format(sql.Identifier(schema)))

    with psycopg.connect(url, row_factory=dict_row, autocommit=autocommit, options=options) as conn:
        yield conn


def fetch_all(query: str | sql.Composable, params: Any = None, *, readonly: bool = False) -> list[dict]:
    with connect(readonly=readonly) as conn:
        return conn.execute(query, params).fetchall()


def fetch_one(query: str | sql.Composable, params: Any = None, *, readonly: bool = False) -> dict | None:
    with connect(readonly=readonly) as conn:
        return conn.execute(query, params).fetchone()


def execute(query: str | sql.Composable, params: Any = None) -> None:
    with connect() as conn:
        conn.execute(query, params)


def _read_sql(name: str) -> str:
    return (SQL_DIR / name).read_text()


def create_target_schema(conn: psycopg.Connection, schema: str) -> None:
    """Create the analytics tables in `schema` (idempotent)."""
    if schema not in (ANALYTICS_SCHEMA, STAGING_SCHEMA):
        raise ValueError(f"not a target schema: {schema}")
    conn.execute(_read_sql("target.sql").replace("__TARGET__", schema))


def rebuild_staging(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> None:
    """Drop and recreate the staging target so each validation starts empty."""
    conn.execute(sql.SQL("DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS {} CASCADE").format(sql.Identifier(STAGING_SCHEMA)))
    create_target_schema(conn, STAGING_SCHEMA)


def _ensure_readonly_role(conn: psycopg.Connection) -> None:
    info = conninfo_to_dict(get_settings().readonly_database_url)
    role, password = info["user"], info["password"]
    exists = conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = %s", (role,)).fetchone()
    verb = sql.SQL("ALTER") if exists else sql.SQL("CREATE")
    conn.execute(
        sql.SQL("{} ROLE {} LOGIN PASSWORD {}").format(verb, sql.Identifier(role), sql.Literal(password))
    )
    for schema in READONLY_SCHEMAS:
        conn.execute(
            sql.SQL("GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA {s} TO {r}; GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA {s} TO {r}").format(
                s=sql.Identifier(schema), r=sql.Identifier(role)
            )
        )


def ensure_schema() -> None:
    """Create every schema, table, and role that is missing (idempotent)."""
    with connect() as conn:
        # Concurrent callers (tests, API startup) would otherwise race on
        # CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS, which is not atomic in PostgreSQL.
        conn.execute("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('dtm_schema'))")
        conn.execute(_read_sql("oltp.sql"))
        conn.execute(_read_sql("pipeline.sql"))
        create_target_schema(conn, ANALYTICS_SCHEMA)
        conn.execute(_read_sql("dtm.sql"))
        _ensure_readonly_role(conn)


def drop_all() -> None:
    """Remove all demo data and state. Used only by the demo reset."""
    with connect() as conn:
        conn.execute("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('dtm_schema'))")
        for schema in (SOURCE_SCHEMA, ANALYTICS_SCHEMA, STAGING_SCHEMA, "pipeline", "dtm"):
            conn.execute(sql.SQL("DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS {} CASCADE").format(sql.Identifier(schema)))

"""Test setup: run everything against a separate database.

Tests reset the demo environment freely, so they must never point at the
database a running demo is using. The same PostgreSQL server is reused with a
dedicated `datatracemind_test` database.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os

import psycopg
import pytest

TEST_DATABASE = "datatracemind_test"
_PORT = os.environ.get("DTM_POSTGRES_PORT", "5432")
_SERVER = f"127.0.0.1:{_PORT}"
_ADMIN = os.environ.get("DTM_TEST_ADMIN_URL", f"REDACTED")


def pytest_configure(config: pytest.Config) -> None:
    # Set before any datatracemind import reads its settings.
    os.environ["DTM_DATABASE_URL"] = f"REDACTED"
    os.environ["DTM_READONLY_DATABASE_URL"] = (
        f"REDACTED"
    )
    os.environ["DTM_BACKGROUND_WORKERS"] = "0"
    os.environ["DTM_AUTO_INVESTIGATE"] = "0"
    os.environ.pop("DTM_DEMO_ACCESS_CODE", None)
    # Tests must not send traces to the project's neatlogs workspace.
    os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"] = ""
    with psycopg.connect(_ADMIN, autocommit=True) as conn:
        exists = conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname = %s", (TEST_DATABASE,)).fetchone()
        if not exists:
            conn.execute(f'CREATE DATABASE "{TEST_DATABASE}"')


@pytest.fixture
def baseline() -> dict:
    """A freshly reset demo environment. Returns the reset report."""
    from datatracemind import demo

    return demo.reset()
=== support.py
"""Test double for the model provider.

`ScriptedProvider` stands in for Codex so that the workflow's control flow and
guardrails can be tested without spending model usage. Its tool calls are
real: it runs the same tool functions against the test database and returns
their results, so evidence in these tests is genuine. Only the role outputs
are scripted, by the test that needs them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel

from datatracemind import db, store
from datatracemind.config import TRANSFORM_FILE
from datatracemind.llm.base import Availability, LLMError, RoleCall, RoleResult
from datatracemind.models import (
    Hypothesis,
    InvestigationReport,
    Observation,
    RepairPlan,
    RootCauseReport,
    TokenUsage,
    ToolCallRecord,
)
from datatracemind.tools.registry import TOOLS
from etl import transform_store

# Arguments each tool is called with when a role's plan requires it.
DEFAULT_ARGUMENTS: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
    "compare_source_target_metrics": {"metric_name": "net_revenue", "time_range": "all"},
    "run_readonly_sql": {"query_template_id": "source_refunds_by_status"},
    "get_etl_code": {"version_or_path": "active"},
    "get_etl_run_logs": {"run_id_or_recent_window": "last_5"},
    "get_source_schema": {"table_name": "orders"},
    "find_missing_source_ids": {"source_table": "orders", "target_table": "fact_orders"},
    "find_duplicate_business_keys": {"table_name": "fact_payments", "key_columns": ["payment_id"]},
    "get_checkpoint": {"pipeline_name": "order_revenue"},
}

Step = Callable[[RoleCall], BaseModel]


def call_tool(tool: str, arguments: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> ToolCallRecord:
    arguments = DEFAULT_ARGUMENTS[tool] if arguments is None else arguments
    try:
        result = TOOLS[tool].fn(**arguments)
    except Exception as exc:
        return ToolCallRecord(tool=tool, arguments=arguments, status="failed", error=str(exc))
    return ToolCallRecord(tool=tool, arguments=arguments, result=result, status="completed")


class ScriptedProvider:
    """Runs each role's required tools for real, then returns the scripted output.

    `script` maps a role to a list of steps consumed one per turn. A step is a
    function of the RoleCall that returns the role's output or raises LLMError.
    A role with no steps left uses its default output.
    """

    name = "scripted"
    model = "test-model"

    def __init__(self, script: dict[str, list[Step]] | None = None, *, available: bool = True) -> None:
        self.script = {role: list(steps) for role, steps in (script or {}).items()}
        self.available = available
        self.calls: list[RoleCall] = []

    def availability(self) -> Availability:
        if self.available:
            return Availability(True, "api_key", "scripted provider")
        return Availability(False, "none", "Install the Codex CLI and run `codex login`, or set CODEX_API_KEY.")

    def estimate_cost(self, usage: TokenUsage) -> float:
        return usage.input_tokens / 1_000_000

    def run_turn(self, call: RoleCall) -> RoleResult:
        self.calls.append(call)
        usage = TokenUsage(input_tokens=1000, cached_input_tokens=400, output_tokens=100)
        tool_calls = [call_tool(tool) for tool in call.required_tools]
        if call.role == "targeted_investigator":
            tool_calls.append(call_tool("get_checkpoint"))
        steps = self.script.get(call.role) or []
        step = steps.pop(0) if steps else DEFAULT_STEPS[call.role]
        try:
            output = step(call)
        except LLMError as exc:
            exc.tool_calls, exc.usage = tool_calls, usage
            raise
        return RoleResult(
            output=output, tool_calls=tool_calls, usage=usage, duration_s=0.01, model=self.model,
            reasoning_effort="none", est_cost_usd=self.estimate_cost(usage),
        )  # fmt: skip

    def turns(self, role: str) -> int:
        return sum(1 for call in self.calls if call.role == role)


# --- Scripted outputs --------------------------------------------------------


def report(_: RoleCall) -> InvestigationReport:
    return InvestigationReport(
        observations=[Observation(statement="see the recorded tool results", tool="(scripted)")], open_questions=[]
    )


def evidence_ids() -> list[str]:
    """IDs of all evidence filed for the (single) incident under test."""
    return [row["evidence_id"] for row in db.fetch_all("SELECT evidence_id FROM dtm.evidence ORDER BY evidence_id")]


def diagnosis(
    category: str = "refund_logic",
    *,
    confirmed: bool = True,
    confidence: float = 0.9,
    cite: Callable[[], list[str]] = evidence_ids,
    needs_more_evidence: bool = False,
    ambiguity: str = "",
) -> Step:
    def step(_: RoleCall) -> RootCauseReport:
        cited = cite()
        return RootCauseReport(
            hypotheses=[
                Hypothesis(
                    hypothesis_id="H1", category=category, statement="scripted leading hypothesis",
                    confidence=confidence, supporting_evidence=cited, contradicting_evidence=[], reasoning="scripted",
                ),
                Hypothesis(
                    hypothesis_id="H2", category="unknown", statement="scripted alternative", confidence=0.1,
                    supporting_evidence=[], contradicting_evidence=cited[:1], reasoning="scripted",
                ),
            ],
            selected_hypothesis_id="H1" if confirmed else "",
            confirmed=confirmed,
            root_cause_summary="scripted root cause",
            implicated_component=f"{TRANSFORM_FILE}: revenue.refund_statuses",
            needs_more_evidence=needs_more_evidence,
            requested_diagnostics=["read the pipeline checkpoint"] if needs_more_evidence else [],
            business_rule_ambiguity=ambiguity,
        )  # fmt: skip

    return step


def repair(*replacements: tuple[str, str], target_file: str = TRANSFORM_FILE, can_repair: bool = True) -> Step:
    """A repair that edits the deployed transformation by plain replacement."""

    def step(_: RoleCall) -> RepairPlan:
        content = transform_store.get_active().content
        for old, new in replacements:
            assert content.count(old) == 1, f"{old!r} is not in the deployed transformation exactly once"

"""Test double for the model provider.

`ScriptedProvider` stands in for Codex so that the workflow's control flow and
guardrails can be tested without spending model usage. Its tool calls are
real: it runs the same tool functions against the test database and returns
their results, so evidence in these tests is genuine. Only the role outputs
are scripted, by the test that needs them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from collections.abc import Callable
from typing import Any

from pydantic import BaseModel

from datatracemind import db, store
from datatracemind.config import TRANSFORM_FILE
from datatracemind.llm.base import Availability, LLMError, RoleCall, RoleResult
from datatracemind.models import (
    Hypothesis,
    InvestigationReport,
    Observation,
    RepairPlan,
    RootCauseReport,
    TokenUsage,
    ToolCallRecord,
)
from datatracemind.tools.registry import TOOLS
from etl import transform_store

# Arguments each tool is called with when a role's plan requires it.
DEFAULT_ARGUMENTS: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {
    "compare_source_target_metrics": {"metric_name": "net_revenue", "time_range": "all"},
    "run_readonly_sql": {"query_template_id": "source_refunds_by_status"},
    "get_etl_code": {"version_or_path": "active"},
    "get_etl_run_logs": {"run_id_or_recent_window": "last_5"},
    "get_source_schema": {"table_name": "orders"},
    "find_missing_source_ids": {"source_table": "orders", "target_table": "fact_orders"},
    "find_duplicate_business_keys": {"table_name": "fact_payments", "key_columns": ["payment_id"]},
    "get_checkpoint": {"pipeline_name": "order_revenue"},
}

Step = Callable[[RoleCall], BaseModel]


def call_tool(tool: str, arguments: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> ToolCallRecord:
    arguments = DEFAULT_ARGUMENTS[tool] if arguments is None else arguments
    try:
        result = TOOLS[tool].fn(**arguments)
    except Exception as exc:
        return ToolCallRecord(tool=tool, arguments=arguments, status="failed", error=str(exc))
    return ToolCallRecord(tool=tool, arguments=arguments, result=result, status="completed")


class ScriptedProvider:
    """Runs each role's required tools for real, then returns the scripted output.

    `script` maps a role to a list of steps consumed one per turn. A step is a
    function of the RoleCall that returns the role's output or raises LLMError.
    A role with no steps left uses its default output.
    """

    name = "scripted"
    model = "test-model"

    def __init__(self, script: dict[str, list[Step]] | None = None, *, available: bool = True) -> None:
        self.script = {role: list(steps) for role, steps in (script or {}).items()}
        self.available = available
        self.calls: list[RoleCall] = []

    def availability(self) -> Availability:
        if self.available:
            return Availability(True, "api_key", "scripted provider")
        return Availability(False, "none", "Install the Codex CLI and run `codex login`, or set CODEX_API_KEY.")

    def estimate_cost(self, usage: TokenUsage) -> float:
        return usage.input_tokens / 1_000_000

    def run_turn(self, call: RoleCall) -> RoleResult:
        self.calls.append(call)
        usage = TokenUsage(input_tokens=1000, cached_input_tokens=400, output_tokens=100)
        tool_calls = [call_tool(tool) for tool in call.required_tools]
        if call.role == "targeted_investigator":
            tool_calls.append(call_tool("get_checkpoint"))
        steps = self.script.get(call.role) or []
        step = steps.pop(0) if steps else DEFAULT_STEPS[call.role]
        try:
            output = step(call)
        except LLMError as exc:
            exc.tool_calls, exc.usage = tool_calls, usage
            raise
        return RoleResult(
            output=output, tool_calls=tool_calls, usage=usage, duration_s=0.01, model=self.model,
            reasoning_effort="none", est_cost_usd=self.estimate_cost(usage),
        )  # fmt: skip

    def turns(self, role: str) -> int:
        return sum(1 for call in self.calls if call.role == role)

def report(_: RoleCall) -> InvestigationReport:
    return InvestigationReport(
        observations=[Observation(statement="see the recorded tool results", tool="(scripted)")], open_questions=[]
    )

    """IDs of all evidence filed for the (single) incident under test."""
    return [row["evidence_id"] for row in db.fetch_all("SELECT evidence_id FROM dtm.evidence ORDER BY evidence_id")]


def diagnosis(
    category: str = "refund_logic",
    *,
    confirmed: bool = True,
    confidence: float = 0.9,
    cite: Callable[[], list[str]] = evidence_ids,
    needs_more_evidence: bool = False,
    ambiguity: str = "",
) -> Step:
    def step(_: RoleCall) -> RootCauseReport:
        cited = cite()
        return RootCauseReport(
            hypotheses=[
                Hypothesis(
                    hypothesis_id="H1", category=category, statement="scripted leading hypothesis",
                    confidence=confidence, supporting_evidence=cited, contradicting_evidence=[], reasoning="scripted",
                ),
                Hypothesis(
                    hypothesis_id="H2", category="unknown", statement="scripted alternative", confidence=0.1,
                    supporting_evidence=[], contradicting_evidence=cited[:1], reasoning="scripted",
                ),
            ],
            selected_hypothesis_id="H1" if confirmed else "",
            confirmed=confirmed,
            root_cause_summary="scripted root cause",
            implicated_component=f"{TRANSFORM_FILE}: revenue.refund_statuses",
            needs_more_evidence=needs_more_evidence,
            requested_diagnostics=["read the pipeline checkpoint"] if needs_more_evidence else [],
            business_rule_ambiguity=ambiguity,
        )  # fmt: skip

    return step

    """A repair that edits the deployed transformation by plain replacement."""

    def step(_: RoleCall) -> RepairPlan:

            escalation_reason="" if can_repair else "the source stopped producing data",
            target_file=target_file,

            rationale="scripted rationale",
            risk="low",
            rollback_plan="redeploy the previous version",
            affected_metrics=["daily_revenue.net_revenue"],
            regression_cases=["partial refund", "pending refund"],
        )

    return step


def raises(error: LLMError) -> Step:
    def step(_: RoleCall) -> BaseModel:
        raise error

    return step


FIX = {
    "DS-01": ("refund_statuses: [COMPLETED]", "refund_statuses: [SUCCEEDED]"),
    "DS-02": ("amount_column: total_amount", "amount_column: order_total"),
    "DS-03": ("payment_join: inner", "payment_join: left"),
    "DS-04": ("mode: append", "mode: replace_by_key"),
    "DS-07": ("timezone: UTC", "timezone: Asia/Kolkata"),
    "DS-16": ("refund_amount_basis: order_total", "refund_amount_basis: refund_amount"),
    "DS-17": ("payment_statuses: [CAPTURED, FAILED]", "payment_statuses: [CAPTURED]"),
}
# Root-cause category a correct diagnosis of each repairable scenario names.
CATEGORY = {
    "DS-01": "refund_logic",
    "DS-02": "schema_drift",
    "DS-03": "join_loss",
    "DS-04": "duplicate_load",
    "DS-07": "timezone",

    "source_investigator": report,
    "pipeline_investigator": report,
    "targeted_investigator": report,
    "root_cause_analyst": diagnosis(),
    "repair_agent": repair(FIX["DS-01"]),
}


def incident(incident_id: str) -> dict:
    return store.get_incident(incident_id)

# DataTraceMind

An agentic data-reliability engineer. It detects when a data pipeline is
producing wrong numbers, investigates the cause with evidence from the source
database, the pipeline, the analytics target, and the approved business
rules, proposes a minimal repair, proves that repair in staging, and applies
it only after a human approves that exact change.

The failure it is built around is the silent one: the ETL job reports
`SUCCESS` while the revenue it loaded is wrong.

Built for neatHack (10–12 October 2026). The build log and submission
evidence are in [hackathon.md](hackathon.md).

## What happens in one incident

1. A simulator writes orders, payments, and refunds to PostgreSQL (`oltp`).
2. A Python ETL loads the analytics schema, driven by a versioned
   transformation file.
3. The Scenario Lab, a separate page for whoever operates the demo, injects
   one known fault.
4. Deterministic quality checks fail and the monitor opens an incident. No
   model decides that something is wrong.
5. A supervisor runs the agent roles: a source-data investigator and a
   pipeline investigator in parallel, a contract lookup, a root-cause analyst,
   and a repair agent. Each model-backed role is one model turn with its own
   tool allow-list and output schema.
6. The repair is run in a staging schema against regression fixtures and every
   quality check, and the load is replayed to prove a retry changes nothing.
7. A person reviews the evidence, diff, and staging result, then approves or
   rejects. Approval is bound to the patch hash.
8. On approval the patch is applied, the pipeline reruns, and the incident
   resolves only if every check passes. Otherwise it rolls back.

## Run it

Requirements: Docker, Python 3.13, Node.js 22 or newer, and a
`LITELLM_API_KEY` for the neatlogs LiteLLM gateway
(<https://neatlogs.com/hackathon/models>) in `.env`. The model defaults to
`claude-sonnet-4.6`; set `LITELLM_MODEL` to use another gateway model. The
earlier Codex CLI provider is still available with `DTM_LLM_PROVIDER=codex`.
Without model credentials everything except "Investigate" still works; that
button is refused with a message saying why.

```sh
cp .env.example .env                  # add LITELLM_API_KEY, and NEATLOGS_API_KEY to trace runs
docker compose up -d postgres
python3.13 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
(cd frontend && npm install && npm run build)
.venv/bin/uvicorn datatracemind.api.app:app --port 8000
```

The first start seeds a deterministic baseline. There are two pages:

| Page | URL | What it is for |
|---|---|---|
| Incident console | <http://127.0.0.1:8000/> | The product: data trust, incidents, evidence, repair review and approval, audit log |
| Scenario Lab | <http://127.0.0.1:8000/lab/> | Operating the demo environment: live traffic, fault injection, reset |

The console never injects anything and is never told what was injected; the
lab never investigates. Each links to the other.

Demo path: in the **Scenario Lab**, pick a scenario, read its briefing, and
press **Inject fault**. Follow **Open INC-0001** to the console, then
**Investigate → review the repair → Approve and apply**. Back in the lab,
**Reset to baseline** returns to the clean state. An investigation takes about
a minute and four model turns.

Live traffic is optional. **Start traffic** in the lab keeps simulated
customers writing orders, payments, and refunds to the source at a chosen rate
(light, steady, or busy); **Send 25 now** writes one batch instead. Every
scenario also reproduces on the seeded baseline with traffic paused, and a
reset pauses it so each run starts from the same data.

For frontend development, `npm run dev` in `frontend/` serves both pages on
port 5173 (`/` and `/lab/`) and proxies `/api` to port 8000.

## Scenarios

| ID | Fault | What the checks see | Expected ending |
|---|---|---|---|
| DS-01 | A transformation change stops subtracting completed refunds | ETL green; net revenue overstated by exactly the succeeded refunds | Repair |
| DS-02 | A source migration renames `orders.total_amount` | ETL fails; analytics goes stale | Repair |
| DS-03 | The order fact is built with an inner join to payments | ETL green; orders with no payment are missing | Repair |
| DS-04 | The load becomes append-only, then a retry rereads a loaded batch | The deploy run is clean; the retry duplicates business keys and inflates revenue | Repair |
| DS-06 | The source starts writing refunds with a new status, `CHARGEBACK` | ETL green with rejected rows; those refunds are missing; revenue still reconciles | Escalation |
| DS-07 | Reporting days are assigned in UTC instead of the business timezone | ETL green; currency totals reconcile, individual days do not | Repair |
| DS-09 | `orders.total_amount` becomes nullable and some paid orders lose their amount | ETL green with rejected rows; those orders and their payments are missing | Escalation |
| DS-16 | Every refund subtracts the whole order amount | ETL green; net revenue understated, only on partial refunds | Repair |
| DS-17 | Failed payments count as revenue | ETL green; revenue overstated by exactly the failed payments | Repair |

IDs follow the scenario table in the product brief; DS-16 and DS-17 are
additions to it. DS-04 takes two pipeline runs to show, which the lab performs
and reports. DS-06 and DS-09 have no correct transformation change: the
workflow is expected to say so and hand the incident to a person.

Each scenario carries a briefing for the lab's operator (what it changes,
what you will see, which checks should fail, how it should end) and an answer
key (`ground_truth`) that only the evaluator reads. Neither reaches an agent:
nothing an agent can call imports the scenario package (a test enforces
this), no prompt contains it, and an incident never names its scenario.

## Safety model

- **Agents only read.** The investigation tools connect with a PostgreSQL role
  that can `SELECT` from the source, the analytics target, and the
  transformation history, and nothing else. No tool accepts SQL; queries are
  templates with typed parameters.
- **The model has no shell.** It is offered only the role's allowed
  investigation tools (the Codex provider additionally runs with the shell and
  web search disabled and a read-only sandbox).
- **Evidence comes from tool results.** The adapter runs the tool calls itself
  (or, with Codex, reads them from its event stream) and fails a turn unless
  the role's required calls succeeded. The model's description of a result is never stored as evidence.
- **A repair is data, not code.** It is a new version of one allowlisted file,
  `etl/transforms/order_revenue.yaml`, and is accepted only if it parses
  against a strict schema and changes a handful of lines.
- **Deterministic checks decide.** Staging validation, approval checks, and
  post-fix verification are code. A model's statement that something passed
  proves nothing.
- **A repair must survive a retry.** Staging loads the same rows a second
  time and reruns every check, so a patch that leaves the load non-idempotent
  is rejected even though a fresh staging load of it looks clean.
- **Approval is bound to the patch.** The executor re-reads the proposal, the
  approval, and the validation result and refuses unless all three name the
  same hash and the patch still applies to the deployed version.
- **Prompts are fixed templates.** No text typed into the web application
  reaches a prompt. Mutating routes can require a demo access code, and
  investigations are capped per hour and per day.
- **Unclear business rules go to a human.** A missing contract, or a rule the
  analyst cannot find, escalates the incident instead of being assumed.

## Tests and evaluation

```sh
.venv/bin/python -m pytest                           # 130 tests, about a minute and a half
.venv/bin/python -m datatracemind.evaluation DS-01   # one real run, scored
```

The tests use a separate `datatracemind_test` database and spend no model
usage: the workflow is driven by a scripted stand-in provider whose tool calls
are real. They cover every scenario from injection to its expected ending,
and the blocked paths as well as the happy one: applying without approval, a
changed patch after approval, a patch that failed validation, rejection, and
a failed post-fix verification.

The evaluator resets the demo, injects a scenario, runs a real investigation,
and scores it against the answer key. Results are written to
`evaluation/results/`.

## Layout

```
contracts/        approved business definitions (revenue, orders, source schema)
etl/              pipeline, transformation, quality checks, run log
simulator/        seeded transaction generator
infra/postgres/   schema for source, analytics target, and application state
datatracemind/
  api/            FastAPI routes
  monitoring/     detection and dashboard read models
  scenarios/      fault scenarios, their briefings, and their answer keys
  tools/          read-only investigation tools and the MCP server
  llm/            provider contract, the LiteLLM gateway and Codex adapters
  agents/         role prompts and the role runner
  orchestration/  supervisor state machine and routing
  repair/         proposals, staging validation, approval, executor
  observability/  neatlogs tracing
  evaluation.py   scenario evaluator
frontend/         React: the incident console (/) and the Scenario Lab (/lab/)
tests/
```

## Hackathon tools

- **neatlogs** traces every investigation: one trace per run, a span per role,
  per model turn (with token usage and estimated cost), and per tool call.
  Approval, apply, and verification are traced as guardrail spans in the same
  session.
- **Entire** captures the coding-agent sessions behind each commit.
- **cfo.ai** holds the business plan; the measured cost per investigation
  feeds it.

## Deviations from the plan

- The simulator is Python, not Spring Boot. The `oltp` schema is its only
  interface to the pipeline, so another producer can replace it.
- The analytics target is a PostgreSQL schema, the plan's documented fallback
  to ClickHouse.
- The ETL worker runs as a thread inside the API process rather than as its
  own service.
- Contract lookup runs before the two investigators rather than beside them,
  so a missing definition escalates before any model usage is spent.
- Two database credentials exist (application and read-only), not a third
  repair-only one. The executor's single write is deploying a new version of
  the transformation file.

## Known limitations

- Only DS-01 has been run with the real model so far: three investigations,
  one of them taken through approval, apply, and verification. Every other
  scenario passes end to end with the scripted provider only, so how the real
  model diagnoses DS-02 through DS-17, and whether it escalates DS-06 and
  DS-09 as intended, is not yet known.
- With DS-04 active and live traffic running, the duplication keeps growing:
  each run rereads the last few seconds and appends them again. That is the
  fault behaving as it would in production, not a second fault.
- Cost figures are estimates at API list prices; the model runs on a
  flat-rate ChatGPT plan.
- There is no container image for the API yet, and the stack has not been
  deployed.

from datatracemind.llm.base import (
    Availability,

from datatracemind.models import TokenUsage, ToolCallRecord
from datatracemind.observability import SpanHandle, span
from datatracemind.tools.registry import TOOLS

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Fixed for every call. Changing either makes earlier runs incomparable:
# record the change in hackathon.md and bump the workflow version.
MODEL = "gpt-6-sol"
REASONING_EFFORT = "medium"

MCP_SERVER_NAME = "dtm"
MCP_SERVER_SCRIPT = REPO_ROOT / "datatracemind" / "tools" / "mcp_server.py"
# Read-only settings the tool server may inherit from this process.
FORWARDED_ENV = ("DTM_READONLY_DATABASE_URL", "DTM_POSTGRES_PORT")
# Never handed to the Codex process.
WITHHELD_ENV = ("NEATLOGS_API_KEY", "LITELLM_API_KEY", "DTM_DATABASE_URL", "DTM_DEMO_ACCESS_CODE")

# USD per million tokens (input, cached input, output), API list prices
# published 10 October 2026. ChatGPT Plus is flat-rate, so a figure computed
# from these is an estimate, not a charge.
PRICES_PER_MILLION = {
    "gpt-6-sol": (2.00, 0.20, 10.00),
    "gpt-6-luna": (0.10, 0.01, 0.50),
}

AVAILABILITY_TTL_S = 60.0
STDERR_TAIL_CHARS = 2000
# Optional debugging aid: a directory that receives each turn's raw event
# stream. The events contain tool results, so keep it out of the repository.
EVENT_LOG_ENV = "DTM_CODEX_EVENT_LOG_DIR"


def estimate_cost_usd(model: str, usage: TokenUsage) -> float:
    """Cost of a turn at API list prices. `input_tokens` includes cached ones."""
    fresh, cached, output = PRICES_PER_MILLION.get(model, PRICES_PER_MILLION[MODEL])
    uncached = max(usage.input_tokens - usage.cached_input_tokens, 0)
    return (uncached * fresh + usage.cached_input_tokens * cached + usage.output_tokens * output) / 1_000_000


def strict_schema(model: type[BaseModel]) -> dict:
    """JSON Schema in the strict form Codex's --output-schema accepts."""
    dropped = {"title", "default", "minimum", "maximum"}

    def clean(node: Any) -> Any:
        if isinstance(node, dict):
            return {key: clean(value) for key, value in node.items() if key not in dropped}
        if isinstance(node, list):
            return [clean(item) for item in node]
        return node

    return clean(model.model_json_schema())


def _toml(value: Any) -> str:
    """A string or list of strings as a TOML value (JSON is valid TOML here)."""
    return json.dumps(value)


def _tool_result(item: dict) -> Any:
    """The structured result of a completed mcp_tool_call item."""
    result = item.get("result") or {}
    structured = result.get("structured_content", result.get("structuredContent"))
    if structured is not None:
        # A non-object return value arrives wrapped as {"result": ...}.
        if isinstance(structured, dict) and set(structured) == {"result"}:
            return structured["result"]
        return structured
    for block in result.get("content") or []:
        if block.get("type") == "text":
            try:
                return json.loads(block["text"])
            except (json.JSONDecodeError, TypeError):
                return block.get("text")
    return None


def _tool_error(item: dict) -> str:
    """Why a tool call failed.

    Codex fills `error.message` when it could not make the call (for example
    approval refused). When the tool itself reports an error, `error` is null
    and the message is the text of the result.
    """
    message = (item.get("error") or {}).get("message")
    if message:
        return message
    for block in (item.get("result") or {}).get("content") or []:
        if block.get("type") == "text" and block.get("text"):
            return block["text"]
    return f"tool call ended with status {item.get('status')}"


def _classify_failure(message: str) -> type[LLMError]:
    text = message.lower()
    if any(marker in text for marker in ("usage limit", "rate limit", "quota", "too many requests", "429")):
        return UsageLimitReached

"""stdio MCP server `dtm`: the investigation tools, as served to the model.

The model provider starts this file as a subprocess for each agent turn and
stops it afterwards, so it keeps no state. It holds only read-only tools, and
it refuses to open a read-write database connection at all.

Run by absolute path:  python /abs/path/datatracemind/tools/mcp_server.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

# Started by path from an unrelated working directory, so the repository root
# is not importable until it is added here.
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))

import functools  # noqa: E402
from collections.abc import Callable  # noqa: E402

from mcp.server.mcpserver import MCPServer  # noqa: E402
from mcp.server.mcpserver.exceptions import ToolError as McpToolError  # noqa: E402

from datatracemind import db  # noqa: E402
from datatracemind.tools.investigation import ToolError  # noqa: E402
from datatracemind.tools.registry import TOOLS  # noqa: E402


def _expose(fn: Callable[..., dict]) -> Callable[..., dict]:
    """Let a tool's own refusals reach the model so it can correct the call.

    The server library hides the text of any other exception, which keeps
    database errors and stack details out of the model's context.
    """

    @functools.wraps(fn)
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        try:
            return fn(*args, **kwargs)
        except ToolError as exc:
            raise McpToolError(str(exc)) from exc

    return wrapper


def build_server() -> MCPServer:
    server = MCPServer("dtm", instructions="Read-only diagnostic tools for the order-to-revenue data pipeline.")
    for spec in TOOLS.values():
        server.add_tool(_expose(spec.fn), name=spec.name, description=spec.description, structured_output=True)
    return server


if __name__ == "__main__":
    db.forbid_write_connections()
    build_server().run()

def test_command_carries_every_required_safety_setting(fake_codex, monkeypatch):
    run("ok", monkeypatch)
    recorded = json.loads(fake_codex.read_text())
    argv = recorded["argv"]
    joined = " ".join(argv)
    assert argv[0] == "exec" and argv[-1] == "fixed prompt"
    for flag in ("--json", "--ephemeral", "--skip-git-repo-check", "--ignore-user-config", "--output-schema"):
        assert flag in argv
    assert argv[argv.index("-m") + 1] == "gpt-6-sol"

    assert "mcp_server.py" in joined
    assert "danger" not in joined and "bypass" not in joined and "workspace-write" not in joined
    assert recorded["stdin_closed"] is True
    # Secrets the model process has no use for are withheld from it.
    assert "NEATLOGS_API_KEY" not in recorded["env"] and "DTM_DATABASE_URL" not in recorded["env"]

# Build and test.
#
# Runs on every push to main that changes the application. The backend tests
# run against a throwaway PostgreSQL, and the frontend is built the way the
# deployment builds it. Nothing is deployed from here: the host builds and
# starts the one service itself (see "Deploy" in README.md).
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "datatracemind/**"
      - "etl/**"
      - "simulator/**"
      - "contracts/**"
      - "infra/**"
      - "tests/**"
      - "frontend/**"
      - "requirements.txt"
      - "pytest.ini"
      - ".github/workflows/ci.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build-test:
    name: Build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    services:
      # A database for this job only; tests/conftest.py creates its own
      # datatracemind_test database on this server.
      postgres:
        image: postgres:17-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: dtm_admin
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: REDACTED
          POSTGRES_DB: datatracemind
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U dtm_admin -d datatracemind"
          --health-interval 2s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 30
    env:
      DTM_DATABASE_URL: REDACTED
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "22"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Build
        run: python -m compileall -q datatracemind etl simulator

      - name: Test
        run: python -m pytest

      - name: Build the frontend
        working-directory: frontend
        run: npm ci && npm run build

"""Runtime settings, read from the environment.

`.env` is loaded here so that every entry point (API, ETL, tool server,
scripts) sees the same values. The database is whatever PostgreSQL
DTM_DATABASE_URL names; there is no default.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from psycopg.conninfo import conninfo_to_dict, make_conninfo

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CONTRACTS_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "contracts"
TRANSFORMS_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "etl" / "transforms"
SQL_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "infra" / "postgres"

PIPELINE_NAME = "order_revenue"
# The only file a repair may target, relative to the repository root.
TRANSFORM_FILE = "etl/transforms/order_revenue.yaml"
READONLY_ROLE = "dtm_readonly"


def _flag(name: str, default: bool) -> bool:
    value = os.environ.get(name)
    if value is None:
        return default
    return value.strip().lower() in {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}


def _readonly_url(database_url: str) -> str:
    """The same database, signed in as the read-only role.

    Its password is derived from the application role's, so one connection
    string configures both and the read-only one is never a known default.
    """
    password = conninfo_to_dict(database_url).get("password")
    if not password:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "DTM_DATABASE_URL has no password to derive the read-only role's from; "
            "set DTM_READONLY_DATABASE_URL as well"
        )
    derived = hmac.new(str(password).encode(), READONLY_ROLE.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return make_conninfo(database_url, user=READONLY_ROLE, password=derived)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    # None when unset. The tool server is started with the read-only one only.
    database_url: str | None
    readonly_database_url: str | None
    demo_seed: int
    etl_interval_s: float
    traffic_min_interval_s: float
    traffic_max_interval_s: float
    freshness_objective_s: float
    run_background_workers: bool
    auto_investigate: bool
    demo_access_code: str | None
    investigations_per_hour: int
    investigations_per_day: int


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    load_dotenv(REPO_ROOT / ".env")
    env = os.environ
    database_url = env.get("DTM_DATABASE_URL") or None
    readonly_database_url = env.get("DTM_READONLY_DATABASE_URL") or (
        _readonly_url(database_url) if database_url else None
    )
    return Settings(
        database_url=database_url,
        readonly_database_url=readonly_database_url,
        demo_seed=int(env.get("DTM_DEMO_SEED", "20261010")),
        etl_interval_s=float(env.get("DTM_ETL_INTERVAL_S", "6")),
        traffic_min_interval_s=float(env.get("DTM_TRAFFIC_MIN_INTERVAL_S", "0.5")),
        traffic_max_interval_s=float(env.get("DTM_TRAFFIC_MAX_INTERVAL_S", "2.0")),
        freshness_objective_s=float(env.get("DTM_FRESHNESS_OBJECTIVE_S", "60")),
        run_background_workers=_flag("DTM_BACKGROUND_WORKERS", True),
        auto_investigate=_flag("DTM_AUTO_INVESTIGATE", False),
        demo_access_code=env.get("DTM_DEMO_ACCESS_CODE") or None,
        investigations_per_hour=int(env.get("DTM_INVESTIGATIONS_PER_HOUR", "6")),
        investigations_per_day=int(env.get("DTM_INVESTIGATIONS_PER_DAY", "30")),
    )

toolUseResult.originalFile:
# Build, test, and deploy the backend.
#
# Runs on every push to main that changes a backend file. The commit is tested
# against a fresh PostgreSQL. Only if every test passes is it packed into
# dtm-backend.tar.gz, copied over the previous build in ~/dtm_build/ on the EC2
# host, and started there with start-dtm-service.sh.
#
# Repository settings this workflow reads
# (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions):
#
#   secret    EC2_SSH_KEY   private key (.pem) of the instance's key pair
#   variable  EC2_HOST      public DNS name or IP address of the instance
#   variable  EC2_USER      login user; optional, defaults to ec2-user
#   secret    LITELLM_API_KEY  neatlogs LiteLLM gateway key; written into the
#                              host's .env on every deploy when set
#
# The host must already hold ~/dtm_build/.env, and its security group must
# allow SSH (port 22) from GitHub-hosted runners.
name: Backend deploy

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "datatracemind/**"
      - "etl/**"
      - "simulator/**"
      - "contracts/**"
      - "infra/**"
      - "tests/**"
      - "requirements.txt"
      - "pytest.ini"
      - "docker-compose.yml"
      - "start-dtm-service.sh"
      - ".github/workflows/backend-deploy.yml"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  build-test:
    name: Build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    services:
      # Same image and credentials as docker-compose.yml; tests/conftest.py
      # creates its own datatracemind_test database on this server.
      postgres:
        image: postgres:17-alpine
        env:
          POSTGRES_USER: dtm_admin
          POSTGRES_PASSWORD: REDACTED
          POSTGRES_DB: datatracemind
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
        options: >-
          --health-cmd "pg_isready -U dtm_admin -d datatracemind"
          --health-interval 2s
          --health-timeout 3s
          --health-retries 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version: "3.13"
          cache: pip

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Build
        run: python -m compileall -q datatracemind etl simulator

      - name: Test
        run: python -m pytest

      # Packed from the commit rather than the working tree, so nothing the
      # build or the tests left behind is shipped. start-dtm-service.sh
      # refuses an archive that lacks these paths.
      - name: Package
        run: |
          git archive --format=tar.gz -o dtm-backend.tar.gz HEAD \
            datatracemind etl simulator contracts infra requirements.txt docker-compose.yml

      - name: Keep the build
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: dtm-backend
          path: |
            dtm-backend.tar.gz
            start-dtm-service.sh
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 14

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to EC2
    needs: build-test
    # A manual run on another branch stops after the tests.
    if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # One deploy at a time. A newer one waits for the running one to finish.
    concurrency:
      group: backend-deploy
      cancel-in-progress: false
    env:
      EC2_HOST: ${{ vars.EC2_HOST }}
      EC2_USER: ${{ vars.EC2_USER || 'ec2-user' }}
    steps:
      - name: Download the build
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: dtm-backend

      - name: Set up SSH
        env:
          EC2_SSH_KEY: ${{ secrets.EC2_SSH_KEY }}
        run: |
          if [[ -z "$EC2_HOST" || -z "$EC2_SSH_KEY" ]]; then
            echo "::error::Set the EC2_HOST variable and the EC2_SSH_KEY secret in the repository settings."
            exit 1
          fi
          umask 077
          mkdir -p ~/.ssh
          printf '%s\n' "$EC2_SSH_KEY" > ~/.ssh/dtm_deploy
          # The runner is new on every run, so the host key is taken on first contact.
          if ! ssh-keyscan -T 15 "$EC2_HOST" > ~/.ssh/known_hosts 2>/dev/null || [[ ! -s ~/.ssh/known_hosts ]]; then
            echo "::error::Cannot reach $EC2_HOST on port 22. Check that the instance is running, that EC2_HOST is its current address, and that its security group allows SSH from GitHub Actions."
            exit 1
          fi
          cat > ~/.ssh/config <<EOF
          Host dtm
            HostName $EC2_HOST
            User $EC2_USER
            IdentityFile ~/.ssh/dtm_deploy
            IdentitiesOnly yes
            BatchMode yes
            ConnectTimeout 15
            ServerAliveInterval 30
          EOF

      - name: Replace the build on the host
        run: |
          ssh dtm 'mkdir -p dtm_build'
          scp dtm-backend.tar.gz start-dtm-service.sh dtm:dtm_build/

      # Keys kept as repository secrets are written into the host's .env, so
      # they need not be copied there by hand. A secret that is not set leaves
      # the .env line as it is. Values go over stdin, never on a command line.
      - name: Update settings on the host
        env:
          LITELLM_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.LITELLM_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          for name in LITELLM_API_KEY; do
            value="${!name}"
            [[ -n "$value" ]] || { echo "Secret $name is not set; keeping the host's value."; continue; }
            printf '%s' "$value" | ssh dtm "set -euo pipefail; umask 077
              value=\$(cat)
              touch dtm_build/.env && chmod 600 dtm_build/.env
              { grep -v '^$name=' dtm_build/.env || true; printf '%s=%s\n' '$name' \"\$value\"; } > dtm_build/.env.new
              mv dtm_build/.env.new dtm_build/.env"
            echo "Set $name in dtm_build/.env."
          done

      # A login shell, so the API inherits the same PATH (uv, the Codex CLI)
      # as when the script is run by hand. The script exits non-zero unless
      # /api/health answers, which fails this job.
      - name: Start the services
        run: ssh dtm 'bash -l dtm_build/start-dtm-service.sh'

"""Runtime settings, read from the environment.

`.env` is loaded here so that every entry point (API, ETL, tool server,
scripts) sees the same values. The database is whatever PostgreSQL
DTM_DATABASE_URL names; there is no default.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import hmac
import os
from dataclasses import dataclass
from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv
from psycopg.conninfo import conninfo_to_dict, make_conninfo

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
CONTRACTS_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "contracts"
TRANSFORMS_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "etl" / "transforms"
SQL_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "infra" / "postgres"

PIPELINE_NAME = "order_revenue"
# The only file a repair may target, relative to the repository root.
TRANSFORM_FILE = "etl/transforms/order_revenue.yaml"
READONLY_ROLE = "dtm_readonly"


def _flag(name: str, default: bool) -> bool:
    value = os.environ.get(name)
    if value is None:
        return default
    return value.strip().lower() in {"1", "true", "yes", "on"}


def _readonly_url(database_url: str) -> str:
    """The same database, signed in as the read-only role.

    Its password is derived from the application role's, so one connection
    string configures both and the read-only one is never a known default.
    """
    password = conninfo_to_dict(database_url).get("password")
    if not password:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "DTM_DATABASE_URL has no password to derive the read-only role's from; "
            "set DTM_READONLY_DATABASE_URL as well"
        )
    derived = hmac.new(str(password).encode(), READONLY_ROLE.encode(), hashlib.sha256).hexdigest()
    return make_conninfo(database_url, user=READONLY_ROLE, password=derived)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Settings:
    # None when unset. The tool server is started with the read-only one only.
    database_url: str | None
    readonly_database_url: str | None
    demo_seed: int
    etl_interval_s: float
    traffic_min_interval_s: float
    traffic_max_interval_s: float
    freshness_objective_s: float
    run_background_workers: bool
    auto_investigate: bool
    demo_access_code: str | None
    investigations_per_hour: int
    investigations_per_day: int


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    load_dotenv(REPO_ROOT / ".env")
    env = os.environ
    database_url = env.get("DTM_DATABASE_URL") or None
    readonly_database_url = env.get("DTM_READONLY_DATABASE_URL") or (
        _readonly_url(database_url) if database_url else None
    )
    return Settings(
        database_url=database_url,
        readonly_database_url=readonly_database_url,
        demo_seed=int(env.get("DTM_DEMO_SEED", "20261010")),
        etl_interval_s=float(env.get("DTM_ETL_INTERVAL_S", "6")),
        traffic_min_interval_s=float(env.get("DTM_TRAFFIC_MIN_INTERVAL_S", "0.5")),
        traffic_max_interval_s=float(env.get("DTM_TRAFFIC_MAX_INTERVAL_S", "2.0")),
        freshness_objective_s=float(env.get("DTM_FRESHNESS_OBJECTIVE_S", "60")),
        run_background_workers=_flag("DTM_BACKGROUND_WORKERS", True),
        auto_investigate=_flag("DTM_AUTO_INVESTIGATE", False),
        demo_access_code=env.get("DTM_DEMO_ACCESS_CODE") or None,
        investigations_per_hour=int(env.get("DTM_INVESTIGATIONS_PER_HOUR", "6")),
        investigations_per_day=int(env.get("DTM_INVESTIGATIONS_PER_DAY", "30")),
    )

"""Test setup: run everything against a separate database.

Tests reset the demo environment freely, so they must never point at the
database a running demo is using. They create a dedicated `datatracemind_test`
database on the server that DTM_DATABASE_URL names, or on the one that
DTM_TEST_ADMIN_URL names when the tests should use a different server.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path

import psycopg
import pytest
from dotenv import load_dotenv
from psycopg.conninfo import make_conninfo

TEST_DATABASE = "datatracemind_test"


def pytest_configure(config: pytest.Config) -> None:
    load_dotenv(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / ".env")
    server = os.environ.get("DTM_TEST_ADMIN_URL") or os.environ.get("DTM_DATABASE_URL")
    if not server:
        raise pytest.UsageError(
            "Set DTM_DATABASE_URL (or DTM_TEST_ADMIN_URL) to a PostgreSQL server; "
            f"the tests create their own {TEST_DATABASE} database on it."
        )
    # Set before any datatracemind import reads its settings. An empty value
    # still counts as set, so .env cannot bring back the demo's.
    os.environ["DTM_DATABASE_URL"] = make_conninfo(server, dbname=TEST_DATABASE)
    os.environ["DTM_READONLY_DATABASE_URL"] = ""
    os.environ["DTM_BACKGROUND_WORKERS"] = "0"
    os.environ["DTM_AUTO_INVESTIGATE"] = "0"
    os.environ.pop("DTM_DEMO_ACCESS_CODE", None)
    # Tests must not send traces to the project's neatlogs workspace.
    os.environ["NEATLOGS_API_KEY"] = ""
    with psycopg.connect(server, autocommit=True) as conn:
        exists = conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname = %s", (TEST_DATABASE,)).fetchone()
        if not exists:
            conn.execute(f'CREATE DATABASE "{TEST_DATABASE}"')


@pytest.fixture
def baseline() -> dict:
    """A freshly reset demo environment. Returns the reset report."""
    from datatracemind import demo

    return demo.reset()

from pathlib import Path

p = Path("README.md")
s = p.read_text()

def swap(old, new):
    global s
    assert s.count(old) == 1, old[:60]
    s = s.replace(old, new)

swap('''Requirements: Docker, Python 3.13, Node.js 22 or newer, and a
`LITELLM_API_KEY` for the neatlogs LiteLLM gateway
''', '''Requirements: a PostgreSQL database, Python 3.13, Node.js 22 or newer, and a
`LITELLM_API_KEY` for the neatlogs LiteLLM gateway
''')

swap('''```sh
cp .env.example .env                  # add LITELLM_API_KEY, and NEATLOGS_API_KEY to trace runs
docker compose up -d postgres
python3.13 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
(cd frontend && npm install && npm run build)
.venv/bin/uvicorn datatracemind.api.app:app --port 8000
```

The first start seeds a deterministic baseline. There are two pages:
''', '''The database is any PostgreSQL server, hosted or local: put its connection
string in `.env` as `DTM_DATABASE_URL`. On first start the app creates its
schemas, the seed data, and a read-only role named `dtm_readonly` for the
investigation tools, so the role in the connection string must be allowed to
create roles.

```sh
cp .env.example .env                  # add DTM_DATABASE_URL and LITELLM_API_KEY, and NEATLOGS_API_KEY to trace runs
python3.13 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt
(cd frontend && npm install && npm run build)
.venv/bin/uvicorn datatracemind.api.app:app --port 8000
```

The first start seeds a deterministic baseline. The same process serves the
API and the built frontend, which has two pages:
''')

swap('''For frontend development, `npm run dev` in `frontend/` serves both pages on
port 5173 (`/` and `/lab/`) and proxies `/api` to port 8000.
''', '''For frontend development, `npm run dev` in `frontend/` serves both pages on
port 5173 (`/` and `/lab/`) and proxies `/api` to port 8000.

## Deploy

There is one service to deploy. FastAPI answers `/api` and serves the built
frontend at `/` and `/lab/`; the database is whichever PostgreSQL
`DTM_DATABASE_URL` names.

- **Build:** `pip install -r requirements.txt && (cd frontend && npm ci && npm run build)`
- **Start:** `uvicorn datatracemind.api.app:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT`
- **Health check:** `GET /api/health`
- **Settings:** `DTM_DATABASE_URL`, `LITELLM_API_KEY`, and `DTM_DEMO_ACCESS_CODE`
  (see [.env.example](.env.example) for the rest)

Run exactly one process and keep it running. The ETL worker, the traffic
stream, and running investigations are threads inside it, so a second worker
or a host that starts the app per request would each have their own.
''')

swap('''.venv/bin/python -m pytest                           # 130 tests, about a minute and a half
''', '''.venv/bin/python -m pytest                           # 137 tests, about a minute and a half on a local database
''')

swap('''The tests use a separate `datatracemind_test` database and spend no model
usage: the workflow is driven by a scripted stand-in provider whose tool calls
are real. They cover every scenario from injection to its expected ending,
''', '''The tests never touch the demo's data. They create a separate
`datatracemind_test` database on the server `DTM_DATABASE_URL` names, so its
role must be allowed to create databases; set `DTM_TEST_ADMIN_URL` to run them
on another server. They spend no model usage: the workflow is driven by a
scripted stand-in provider whose tool calls are real. They cover every
scenario from injection to its expected ending,
''')

swap('''- There is no container image for the API yet, and the stack has not been

''', '''- The service is one process and cannot be scaled out: the ETL worker, the

''')
p.write_text(s)
EOF

Running `pytest` needs a PostgreSQL server the tests can create `datatracemind_test` on. No Postgres binaries are installed on this Mac; Docker Desktop is (image `postgres:17-alpine` cached), and a throwaway container is still the way to get one even though the repo itself no longer uses Docker.

**From the `simpler-arch` branch on (2026-10-12):** `tests/conftest.py` takes the server from `DTM_DATABASE_URL` (or `DTM_TEST_ADMIN_URL`, which wins) and no longer reads `DTM_POSTGRES_PORT`. The read-only role's URL is derived, so one variable is enough.

aiTitle: Simplify architecture: remove AWS and Docker

content.text:
The branch is rebased and the simplification is implemented, but it has only been run against a local stand-in database so far, not your hosted one. Nothing is committed yet.

**Rebase:** `simpler-arch` now sits on `origin/main`, which was 4 commits ahead (the LiteLLM provider work). Your local `main` is still 4 behind; I left it alone.

**What changed**
- **AWS removed:** the EC2 deploy job and `start-dtm-service.sh` are gone. The workflow is now [ci.yml](.github/workflows/ci.yml), which only runs the tests and builds the frontend.
- **Docker removed:** `docker-compose.yml` is deleted, and there are no more local database defaults. `DTM_DATABASE_URL` is required and is the only link you need to provide.
- **One deployment:** `frontend/vercel.json` (the proxy to EC2) is deleted. FastAPI serves the console at `/`, the lab at `/lab/` and the API at `/api`. The build and start commands are in a new "Deploy" section of [README.md](README.md).

**Two things I changed beyond the deletions**
